scope: diagnosis only; no persistence, scheduling, queue, retry, thread-count, or durability policy change

diagnostics.counter_layout: one cache-line-aligned counter block per data thread

findings.primary: per-file fsync and its storage-level variability
findings.secondary: full durable-file SHA-256 reread after streaming
findings.tertiary: one persistent pull connection per Worker serializes concurrent outputs from the same Worker
findings.queue_interpretation: a large ready backlog forms, but the queue is not the service work; 16 data threads remain continuously occupied
findings.next_optimization_candidate: none of streaming SHA-256, fdatasync, preallocation or sync_file_range showed a stable matched-load improvement; retain the current path unless a remote production A/B proves otherwise

fsync_contract.reason: requested-output metadata must not commit before delayed local ENOSPC or EIO can be observed
fsync_contract.boundary: local runtime durability only; the containing directory is not fsynced and Controller-host loss, reboot and cross-host durability remain out of scope

followup_optimization_screen.scope: temporary Controller-local /tmp microbenchmarks; 16 threads and 4 GiB per point; no production code change
followup_optimization_screen.fdatasync: indistinguishable from fsync within run variability

measurement_limitations: link_stream_to_fd combines socket read and local write, so stream_seconds cannot split those two operations without changing the transfer implementation

the 1-MiB probe-on/off pair differs by only 0.18 percent, but the 16-MiB probe runs are slower than their adjacent probe-off run; use their repeatable stage proportions for diagnosis and the probe-off run for production throughput
the 64-MiB diagnostic was excluded because Condor could not admit the exact 16-Worker inventory
